text: XY Ltd (XYL) owns a factory. During a severe storm, the floor of the factory is flooded. XYL’s
safety policy is to close the factory until the floor has dried out. However, George, the factory
manager, instructs staff to continue working while the floor is still wet. Jim, one of the workers,
slips and breaks his leg. He is unable to work for several weeks.
Jim reads an article about a serious and incurable illness caused by long-term contact with a
harmful chemical. He realises that he has been exposed to this chemical in XYL’s factory and
he becomes very anxious and depressed. He fears that he might develop the illness as he has
worked at the factory for many years.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
OR
Liz and Kate are writing a book about local historical sites. Sean owns land on which there is an
old castle. Liz and Kate obtain his permission to visit the castle and take photographs. To prepare
for the visit, Liz flies a drone over Sean’s land to film the castle. Sean does not give permission for
the drone flight.
Kate and Liz visit the castle to take photographs. Kate tells Liz that she has heard stories of
treasure buried in the grounds of the castle. Kate takes some tools from her bag and starts to
dig. As she is digging, Sean arrives and tells them both to leave immediately. Liz leaves, but Kate
refuses. Sean grabs Kate and pushes her off his land.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
Section B
Answer two questions from this section.
In an action for negligence, the ‘but for’ test should be the only test applied when assessing
whether causation is present.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
In an action in Rylands v Fletcher, the term ‘non-natural use’ is so vague that it restricts the use of
the tort to a significant extent.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
Equitable remedies are of limited use in the law of tort.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
